_what: Where a footage candidate comes from: the channels whose upload IS the work's own footage (official), and the words in a title that say an upload is somebody's video about the work rather than the work (unofficial). Lists live here, not in scripts/footage_origin.py, because they are appended to as batches show new channels and new kinds of fan upload - that is config work, not code work.
_split: CF-0627 (CF-0561, 2026-10-07): the official channels are the channel's own list - `<root>/channels/<id>/footage-origin.json`, read through the root's shared/channel_data.py by `footage_origin.load_config(channel)`; they moved there unchanged (example-film's, root release/2.3 e693d3e) and are not kept here. What stays here is the rule every channel shares: the `stop_words` that say an upload is somebody's video about the work. `_rule` and `_ids` below describe how both halves are read; the `channels[]` they speak of are in the channel's list.
_rule: A channel on official_channels is official and is never sieved by stop_words - the user's decision of 2026-09-20 is that the official trailer is the most honest source there is, and no word in its title may cost it. Otherwise a stop_words hit makes the upload unofficial and it is dropped from the pool with reason_code 'unofficial_source'. Everything else is unknown: offered, but after every official upload of its own nature.
_ids: CF-0361 (2026-09-24). Officiality is decided by the channel's id, not its name: every entry carries `channels[]` - the YouTube channel ids that ARE this studio or network, each with the call it was resolved by (a `videos.list` on a real upload of a real batch, or `channels.list forHandle`, checked by the title it answered - `@DC` answered 'LOl Rekt' and `@Example Pictures` answered 'lg', and neither went in). An upload that carries `channel_id` is official only when that id is listed here; `pattern` is the fallback for a record without an id (every batch before CF-0361), matched on whole tokens of the channel name (CF-0347: the bare substring 'dc' made every '...Podcast' channel official). `owners` are the names a topic's `title_ref.rights_holder` / `network` is matched against to choose whose upload playlist `fetch_channel_feeds.py` reads deep (default: the pattern itself); `general: true` marks a licensed distributor read for every topic. A new regional channel of a listed studio is added here by id, with the upload it was read off.
_discipline: Every stop word carries `seen_in` - a real upload out of a real batch pool that the word was read off. A word nobody can point at in the data does not go in. Every pattern was replayed over the 46 videos that have ever been fetched as a canonical source (pipeline/*/*/01b-footage-index.json, six batches): the hits are the five this task is about plus eTvRCugVK1Q, and nothing else. The command is in the task file's `## Полный прогон`.
